methods.text: not available for Tennessee: TDOT publishes no crash cost table of its own: HSAM Vol. 2 sends practitioners to the LCCET tool with its 'Fatality, injury, PDO' option (p. 2-74, PDF p. 82) and gives no dollar values; and the public layer has no property-damage crashes outside Nashville, so a cost total would be misleading

not available for Tennessee: TDOT's statewide average crash rates for similar intersections come from TDOT's STID on request (HSAM Vol. 2 p. 2-19, PDF p. 27); no published table, and CrashIQ has no Tennessee traffic counts

Highway Safety Manual (AASHTO, 1st, 2010), Ch. 4, Sec. 4.2.3. Tennessee's own method, TDOT's intersection evaluation compares the crash rate with the statewide average and a critical rate at a 99 percent confidence level (HSAM Vol. 2 p. 2-19, PDF p. 27), isn't built: this report uses the HSM critical rate against the corridor's own sites (national method)

not available for Tennessee: TDOT's intersection evaluation typically uses the most recent three-year period of crashes (HSAM Vol. 2 p. 2-18, PDF p. 26) but sets no minimum for a corridor study; and the public layer starts in 2024
